fields.name: SCP feedback runs
fields.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: During feedback runs each single trial was performed for 8 s.
If a low-frequency tone occurred, the patient was required to move consecutive red arrows upwards by producing cortical negativity (negative SCP trials) (see Fig. 1a).
Analogically, after hearing a high-frequency tone
was asked to move blue arrows downwards which corresponded with suppressing negativity or increasing positivity (positive SCP trials).

Whenever the patient produced the expected SCP shift, he also received a reward in a form of an attractive moving visual-auditory stimulus: a rotating sun animation, green light turning on and applause (Fig. 1a, left top corner).

facts.clinical_statement: Feedback runs of 8 s trials: tone-cued negative or positive SCP shifts moving arrows on a display, with an audio-visual reward

fields.name: SCP feedback display and amplitude reference
fields.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: Red and blue arrows (pointing upwards and downwards, respectively) were shown on the training Visual Display (Fig. 1a).
He was also presented with either two high- or two low-frequency tones. The first and second tone marked the beginning and the end of a trial, respectively.
The arrows appeared every 0.5 s showing momentary amplitude values of the generated SCPs.
The amplitude of the SCP was calculated with reference to a 2 s pre-trial period.
In addition, the mean SCP amplitude value achieved during the whole trial was provided.
was asked to keep the track of the arrows.
was kept informed on his progress in the task.
Values below the arrows on the right side represent the mean amplitude of SCPs generated in a single trial.

facts.clinical_statement: Arrows on the display showed momentary SCP amplitudes every 0.5 s referenced to a 2 s pre-trial period, with two tones marking trial start and end and the mean trial amplitude provided

fields.name: SCP reward threshold setting
fields.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: In the first session of block 1 the SCP amplitude threshold, which the patient had to exceed to be rewarded, was fixed to ensure the level of 30 % successful trials in each run. The value was set separately for positive and negative trials.

In subsequent sessions the thresholds were continuously updated, using mean SCP values obtained in all positive or negative SCP trials completed on the previous day, so that probability of success remained at approximately 30 %.
This approach yielded a stable difficulty levels throughout the whole training.

facts.clinical_statement: Reward thresholds set for about 30 % successful trials and updated each session from the previous day mean SCP values

fields.name: SCP positive-to-negative trial ratio and order
fields.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: In the first training block (block 1) the ratio of positive and negative SCP trials in the run was 1:1. In two remaining blocks (blocks 2 and 3), 66 % were positive SCP trials and 33 % were negative SCP trials (ratio 2:1).

The positive SCP and the negative SCP trials always came in a fixed order. In the training block 1 a positive SCP trial was always followed by a negative SCP trial. In blocks 2 and 3 after two positive SCP trials, a negative SCP trial was presented.
The fixed-order training schedule was applied to facilitate differentiation between the two types of trials.
The 2:1 ratio was set to accelerate the process of elevation of cortical excitation thresholds and, thereby, enhance cortical inhibitory mechanisms

Increasing number of positive trials was intentional since we want to facilitate increasing of the cortical excitation threshold hoping that it helps to attenuate the neuronal synchronization underlying tinnitus and alleviate tinnitus-related symptoms.

facts.clinical_statement: Block 1 used a 1:1 positive-to-negative trial ratio; blocks 2 and 3 used 2:1; trials followed a fixed order

fields.name: SCP transfer runs
fields.subject: index_patient

evidence.quote: During transfer runs no feedback information was provided.
The sun animation and green diode were continuously presented on the Visual Display (Fig. 1b).

Whenever the mean SCP amplitude exceeded the threshold fixed at the level that predicted 30 % successful trials (see above), the sun animation rotated, the diode turned on and the applause sound was produced.

In each training block (1–3), transfer trials constituted the third run and were arranged in a fixed order. In block 1 the ratio of positive SCP trials to negative SCP trials was 1:1, whereas in blocks 2 and 3 the corresponding ratio became 2:1.

facts.clinical_statement: Transfer runs without feedback were the third run of each session, with the same 1:1 then 2:1 ratios

summary.text: A 50-year-old male patient had suffered from chronic tinnitus since 2006, a loud sound in both ears and/or inside the head that became a chronic high-frequency squeak, extremely bothersome, impeding falling asleep and more intensive under stress. He visited a hearing institute in 2007; audiological assessment with MR and CT revealed normal hearing and no organic aetiology. Methods tried over the next 3 years, including tinnitus retraining therapy, were ineffective; he lost his job and did not accept prescribed sedative and SSRI medication.

Standard and high-frequency audiometry showed normal thresholds in both ears, the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory score was 40 of 100, and the Beck Depression Inventory score was 9 of 63, indicating a lack of depressive symptoms. Before the training he was in relatively good health and used no medication; his tinnitus resembled a pure tone of 12 kHz at 40 dB HL and the overall Tinnitus Functional Index score was 45 points.

SCP neurofeedback training began at the institute in 2013 and comprised three 2-week blocks of ten 1.5-hour sessions separated by breaks of about 1 month, with feedback and transfer runs and a positive-to-negative trial ratio of 1:1 in block 1 and 2:1 in blocks 2 and 3. Daily mean SCP amplitudes of positive and negative trials were recorded for each block; he was encouraged to train at home between blocks and practiced self-regulation skills outside the institute.

After the training tinnitus was still present, but the patient reported lower pitch and loudness, better sleep, more control and improved daily life. Matched tinnitus pitch fell to 11 kHz and intensity to 30 dB HL, and the overall TFI score fell from 45 to 6 points. QEEG showed decreased delta, theta and alpha amplitudes in left-hemisphere regions and increased high beta amplitude at T6 and T3 in the eyes-open recording.
